title: Iterative Solvers for Linear Systems
description: Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel, SOR, spectral radius and convergence, conjugate gradients.
html:
🔁 Iterative Solvers for Linear Systems

1. Splitting and Methods

$A = D + L + U$ (diagonal, strictly lower, strictly upper – not the LU factors!).

$$\text{Jacobi: } x_i^{(k+1)} = \tfrac{1}{a_{ii}}\Bigl(b_i - \sum_{j\ne i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\Bigr), \qquad \text{Gauss–Seidel: } x_i^{(k+1)} = \tfrac{1}{a_{ii}}\Bigl(b_i - \sum_{ji}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\Bigr)$$

Example $4x_1 + x_2 = 1$, $2x_1 + 5x_2 = 2$, start $0$

Jacobi: $(0.25, 0.4), (0.15, 0.3), (0.175, 0.34)$. Gauss–Seidel: $(0.25, 0.3), (0.175, 0.33), (0.1675, 0.333)$. Exact $(\frac16, \frac13)$.

2. Convergence

$$x^{(k+1)} = Mx^{(k)} + c, \quad M_J = -D^{-1}(L+U),\; M_{GS} = -(D+L)^{-1}U; \qquad \text{convergence} \iff \rho(M) < 1$$

  • Sufficient: $\|M\| < 1$; strict diagonal dominance $\Rightarrow$ Jacobi and Gauss–Seidel converge; spd $\Rightarrow$ Gauss–Seidel.
  • Diagonal dominance is not necessary. Row swaps can establish it.
  • A priori: $\|x^{(k)} - x^*\| \le \frac{q^k}{1-q}\|x^{(1)} - x^{(0)}\|$, a posteriori: $\frac{q}{1-q}\|x^{(k)} - x^{(k-1)}\|$.
  • Example: $\rho(M_J) = 0.316$, $\rho(M_{GS}) = 0.1 = \rho(M_J)^2$.

3. SOR and CG

$$\text{SOR: } x_i^{(k+1)} = (1-\omega)x_i^{(k)} + \omega\,x_i^{\text{GS}}, \quad \omega_{\text{opt}} = \frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-\rho_J^2}}$$

CG (spd): $\alpha_k = \frac{r_k^Tr_k}{p_k^TAp_k}$, $\beta_k = \frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k}$, $p_{k+1} = r_{k+1} + \beta_kp_k$; $A$-orthogonal directions, exact after $n$ steps.

4. Stopping and Cost

  • Stopping: relative change, relative residual – but residual $\ne$ error (conditioning!).
  • Cost per step $O(\text{nnz})$ instead of $O(n^3)$; storage only for nonzeros.

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Using old instead of new values in Gauss–Seidel.
  • Regarding diagonal dominance as necessary.
  • Confusing the splitting $D, L, U$ with the factors of the LU decomposition.
